title: Oklahoma City's young core flexes growth in statement win over Indiana Pacers
topic: Indiana Pacers at Oklahoma City Thunder
script: Tyrese Haliburton hasn't set foot in Paycom Center since Game 7. He tore his right Achilles that night, and the Pacers lost the 2025 Finals to OKC. Now he's back — not as the franchise savior, but as a question mark in a building that reminded everyone why OKC's young core is ahead of schedule. The Thunder dissected Indiana instead of merely beating them. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander floated on the perimeter, hitting three catch-and-shoot threes in his half, while 7-footer Mara — the No. 12 pick — threw 17 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and four blocks at a Pacers frontcourt still figuring out life without their star. It was a statement. A year ago, OKC won it all on the back of that same youth. Last season, the Spurs took the West. Now the Thunder are sitting at the top of the West again, and the gap between them and the rest — including Indiana — is widening. Here's why it matters: OKC's patience with this young core is the reason they're still here, while Indiana is still waiting on a single night from Haliburton to know what they have. Haliburton may be cleared to play, but the Pacers are still searching for an identity. OKC isn't. Watch whether Haliburton can actually suit up Tuesday — because if he can't, this rematch becomes a referendum on whether Indiana's window ever really existed at all.
